summary: CCC-era 1938 lookout tower in Medicine Bow National Forest, rebuilt as a taller R-6 tower and opened to public rental in 1997.

facts.design: R-6 tower (41-foot treated-timber, per firelookout.com; Recreation.gov instead says 55 feet)

access.note: Rental tower, drive-up most of the season; June snowdrifts may block the road.

visit.trail_note: Guests may need to pack gear in on foot during early-season snow.

events.note: Original lookout built by CCC crews.
H. Arnold Maves listed as lookout personnel.
Renovated and opened for overnight rental.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register January 3, 2015.

evidence.supports: Both the initial build year and the eventual tower swap after about three decades.
evidence.quote: The original fire lookout was constructed during the summer of 1938 by workers employed through the New Deal's Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC). After thirty years of use, it was replaced with a taller, more structurally sound tower.

evidence.supports: Current structure description and 1950 staffer name.
evidence.quote: 1930s: 30' pole L-4 tower. Replaced by the present 41' treated timber R-6 tower. It is available on the Recreation Rental program. Known lookout personnel: 1950: H. Arnold Maves.
The new 55-foot tall tower was used as a fire lookout until the 1990s when it was renovated and opened to the public for overnight rental in 1997.

evidence.supports: NHLR registration date, elevation, administering agency.
evidence.quote: Date Registered January 3, 2015 ... Elevation 9,997 ft (3,047 m) ... Administered by U.S. Forest Service

evidence.supports: Condition and maintenance notes from the 2004 and 2008 site visits.
evidence.quote: July 4, 2004: Joshua Nigro. Needs paint? Yes. Shutters OK? Yes. Condition of wood OK? Yes. Stairs OK? Yes. Glass intact? Yes. Good condition? Yes. Comments: ...the public doing a great job in respecting the tower site... Also the tail to the original tower needs some chainsaw work. Also I raked up around the old outhouse on the west slope and was able to secure that door with some rocks. June 24, 2008: Susan. Needs paint? Yes. Shutters OK? Yes. Condition of wood OK? Yes. Stairs OK? Yes. Glass intact? Yes. Good condition? Yes. Comments: Wonderful experience overall. Should be told either that the refrigerator is broken or how to start it.
The lookout is accessible by car...Guests can drive directly to the lookout most of the season.

corrections.proposed: null (sources disagree: ~16.8 m / 55 ft per Recreation.gov vs. ~12.5 m / 41 ft per firelookout.com, for the current tower)
corrections.why: 9.1 m (about 30 ft) matched the description of the original 1930s pole tower, not the present replacement structure. Applied during 2026-10-04 verification: height_m set to null rather than picking one unverified figure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Recreation.gov and firelookout.com agree the current tower replaced an earlier 1930s structure, but neither gives a precise year for the replacement; this story reports the original 1938 build and notes the later swap without inventing a year for it.

notes_for_editor: Height_m in the record (9.1 m / ~30 ft) likely describes the original 1930s pole tower rather than the current 41-55 ft structure; worth checking against a primary USFS record before correcting. Exact year of the tower replacement (after the original 1938 build) is not pinned down by any source consulted.
